terms.sub: Gross structure of a long bone
clues: A structural region of a growing long bone.
It is bounded by growth plates or ends of the bone.
It is the tubular shaft of a long bone.

terms.sub: Gross structure of a long bone
clues: An end segment of a developing long bone.
It typically participates in joint articulation.
It is one of the expanded ends of a long bone.
Microscopic collagen bundles found in bone attachments.
They anchor the outer bone membrane into underlying lamellae.
They are perforating fibers passing from periosteum into bone.
A thin osteogenic lining inside bone.
It covers internal bone trabeculae and canal walls.
It lines the medullary cavity of a bone.
A process of bone formation during embryonic development.
It builds bone directly without a cartilage intermediate.
It forms flat skull vault bones from mesenchyme.
A developmental mechanism of bone formation.
It uses a temporary cartilage model that gets replaced by bone.
It forms most long bones by replacing hyaline cartilage.
A primary blood vessel supplying a long bone.
It enters through a dedicated foramen along the shaft.
It supplies the medullary cavity and inner bone cortex.
A joint category defined by its uniting tissue.
It lacks a synovial cavity and uses cartilage.
It is a primary cartilaginous joint made of hyaline cartilage.
A midline joint with limited movement and strong fibrocartilage.
The pubic joint and intervertebral discs are examples.
It is a secondary cartilaginous joint with a fibrocartilage pad.
A viscous body fluid confined within a joint cavity.
It helps nourish avascular cartilage inside movable joints.
It lubricates articular surfaces inside a synovial joint.
A freely movable articulation with a single axis of rotation.
It permits motion mainly in one plane such as flexion and extension.
The elbow humeroulnar articulation is this type of joint.
A uniaxial joint specialized for rotational movement.
A bony projection turns inside a ring of bone and ligament.
The atlantoaxial joint where the dens rotates is this type.
An anatomical principle linking muscles, joints, and nerves.
It helps explain why joint pain can refer to nearby regions.
Nerves moving a joint also supply its capsule and overlying skin.
A small closed sac located near sites of mechanical friction.
It cushions gliding tendons or skin over bony prominences.
It is a fluid-filled sac that reduces friction around joints.
